reasoning_traces.think:
The core innovation lies in distilling deep reinforcement learning (DRL) policies into interpretable linear model trees (LMTs). The LMT mimics the DRL’s soft label outputs, where each leaf node encodes a linear regression ŷ = Σ(wᵢ·xᵢ) + b. This enables GSE to reason about game states using structured decision rules rather than opaque neural weights. The method uses variance reduction and t-tests for fast split selection, improving scalability. Counterfactual action replacement augments training data by substituting actions, exposing the model to rare but informative scenarios. These primitives jointly enable GSI to perform Bayesian inference on policy outcomes and GSE to execute real-time tactical decisions based on learned state-action mappings. However, leakage risks persist if features like event duration are misused, and temporal ordering of episodes may introduce bias. The fidelity metrics show strong performance in hockey action values (RMSE ≈ 0.012), suggesting robustness in structured domains.
